title: Detection of a High-velocity Jet from MWC 349A Traced by Hydrogen Recombination Line Maser Emission
question: What are the spatial distribution and kinematics of the H26alpha and H30alpha radio recombination line masers and millimeter continuum emission in MWC 349A, particularly in the high-velocity wind?

data.bands: Band 6 (1.4 mm) and Band 7 (0.8 mm / 0.87 mm)
data.angular_resolution: 0.075'' x 0.025'' (Band 6 continuum) and 0.107'' x 0.051'' (Band 7 continuum); ~0.03'' (H30alpha) and ~0.1'' (H26alpha)

what.value: Continuum angular size and flux density measurements versus frequency from VLA observations

evidence.quote: Figure [2](#fig:scalingrelations) shows the angular size and the flux versus frequency, including the data points reported in (cite: tafoya2004).

what.value: Disk inclination angle of 9 degrees from the line of sight / PA around 98 degrees

evidence.quote: Others (cite: rodriguez2007; baez-rubio2013) have estimated this inclination angle to be around 98$^{\circ}$ in PA; our 1.4mm continuum image above appears to be consistent with this finding.

Since the disk is nearly edge-on with an inclination angle of 9$^{\circ}$ from the LOS, the space velocity of these maser features can be as high as $V_{LOS}/$sin(9$^{\circ}$), or up to 575 km s$^{-1}$
At an estimated distance of 1.2 kpc from the Sun (cite: cohen1985), it is believed to be a hot, massive B\[e\] star (cite: merrill1933)

recipe.goal: Model continuum image morphology and determine astrometric reference centers
recipe.method: Fit 2D elliptical Gaussian models to the Band 6 and Band 7 continuum images and quadratically subtract the synthesized beam to obtain deconvolved sizes and continuum centroid positions
assumptions: Band 6 and Band 7 continuum emissions trace nearly the same material and share a common physical center

recipe.goal: Derive total continuum flux densities, angular sizes, and frequency scaling relations from visibilities
recipe.method: Perform linear regression on visibility amplitude versus projected baseline distance V(b) = S_nu(1 - A b) for short baselines, compute angular size Theta = 1.19e5 A, and fit power-law scaling relations combining ALMA, SMA, and literature VLA measurements
key_parameters: Baseline cutoff < 500,000 wavenumbers for visibility linear regression
assumptions: Spherically symmetric ionized wind source extending to infinity

recipe.goal: Extract 2D positions and intensities of H30alpha and H26alpha masers across velocity channels
recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian to each spectral channel image of the H30alpha and H26alpha cubes to measure centroid positions and peak amplitudes, register offsets relative to the respective band's continuum centroid, and combine fit errors in quadrature with bandpass phase calibration positional errors
key_parameters: Channel width = 1.26 km s^-1; bandpass positional error = 0.042 mas (Band 6, SNR = 470 on J2148+0657) and 0.038 mas (Band 7, SNR = 1400 on J2253+161)
assumptions: Single 2D Gaussian per velocity channel represents the centroid of the maser emission at that velocity

recipe.goal: Fit disk geometry, kinematics, enclosed stellar mass, and deprojected jet velocity
recipe.method: Perform linear least-squares fits to disk masers (-12 to 28 km s^-1) in sky coordinates to determine disk PA and polar axis, fit linear position-velocity relations to derive systemic velocity and velocity-distance slopes, calculate enclosed mass from Keplerian thin-annulus relation V_LOS = sqrt(GM/R^3) l, and deproject polar maser velocities using disk inclination
key_parameters: Disk velocity range: -12 to 28 km s^-1; maser spatial extent (diameter 2R): 45 mas (H26alpha) and 54 mas (H30alpha); distance = 1.2 kpc; inclination = 9 deg from LOS
assumptions: Perfectly edge-on Keplerian disk with H26alpha and H30alpha masers localized on two thin annuli of fixed radii equal to the spatial extent of the masers; high-velocity masers distributed along the polar axis at 9 deg inclination from LOS

Minor deductions for missing CASA version, CLEAN imaging parameters (cell size, thresholds), and unstated continuum subtraction details for the line cubes.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data from a single ALMA project (2017.1.00404.S) on a very bright target (MWC 349A) with a straightforward analysis pipeline (self-calibration, imaging, per-channel 2D Gaussian centroid fitting, and linear fits to position-velocity diagrams) yielding clear, quantitative answer keys (continuum fluxes/sizes, disk PA, systemic velocity, PV slopes, enclosed mass, and polar jet maser offsets).
